statement: Nine generic points of C² lie on exactly 1,442 four-bar coupler curves.

answer.text: Theorem 1.1 proves exactly 1,442 coupler curves, equivalently 8,652 labelled mechanisms, by matching certified upper and lower bounds.
answer.display: Theorem 1.1 proves exactly 1,442 coupler curves, equivalently 8,652 labelled mechanisms, by matching certified upper and lower bounds.

source.version: arXiv:2609.22003v1, submitted 18 September 2026; 32-page PDF and corresponding arXiv HTML checked.

notes:
Computer-assisted proof in a preprint. Full-text argument and certification descriptions checked; auxiliary certificates were not independently rerun. No maximum-real count is established.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_5785404dad27fc44; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

The upper bound subtracts at least 4,096 certified escaping branches from a mixed-volume count of 5,538. The lower bound uses 8,652 certified distinct regular labelled-mechanism solutions and the generic sixfold mechanism-to-curve correspondence. The proof also verifies that its chart misses no relevant generic curves.

Supporting source locations. Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.9 (p.12); Lemma 3.11 (p.13); Proposition 6.1, Corollary 6.2 and Lemma 6.3 (p.27); proof of Theorem 1.1 (pp.27–28). Certification procedure: Section 5.3 (pp.24–25), Section 6 and Table 1 (pp.25–26). Printed page numbers equal PDF page index +1.
scope: Nondegenerate complex planar four-bar coupler curves through nine generic points of C^2; curves rather than labelled mechanisms are counted.
